subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What different themes do students raise in these open responses?

judge.implied_focus: Themes in students' open responses about their remote/online learning experience

per_column.name: engagement_participation
per_column.rationale: A coherent facet: student engagement as a theme in remote learning responses.

per_column.name: hands_on_materials_impact
per_column.rationale: Captures a distinct theme around hands-on/lab materials in remote contexts.

per_column.name: subject_remote_fit
per_column.rationale: How well subjects fit remote delivery; coherent facet.

per_column.name: cognitive_depth_understanding
per_column.rationale: Near-duplicate of cognitive_depth with overlapping values; redundant, not a distinct facet.

per_column.name: instructional_quality_variation
per_column.rationale: Duplicate of instructional_quality; adds no new theme.

judge.rationale: The columns collectively centre coherently on a single inferable focus -- themes in students' open responses about remote/online learning -- with a well-differentiated, thematically categorical structure (engagement, materials, community, instruction, subject fit, equity, wellbeing, cognitive depth, innovation). This is a strong, coherent focus and clearly actionable for an analyst. However, structure quality is materially undermined: six of the fifteen columns are near-exact duplicates of earlier ones (cognitive_depth_understanding, instructional_quality_variation, peer_interaction_community_loss, household_equity_gaps, pedagogical_innovation_success, student_wellbeing_anxiety), sharing the same value vocabularies and only trivially shifted counts. This redundancy inflates the schema without adding analytical facets, weakening the otherwise sound multi-facet decomposition.
